newsitem.title: CHINA: Statue of China's Deng not to tower over HK.
newsitem.headline: Statue of China's Deng not to tower over HK.

text.p: Death prevented China's late leader Deng Xiaoping from witnessing the return of Hong Kong to Beijing next week and now China's only planned statue of the architect of reform will also miss the show.

Chinese authorities had planned to erect a huge bronze statue of the reformer -- whose negotiations with Britain in the 1980s cemented the handover of Hong Kong on July 1 -- in the southern boomtown of Shenzhen that borders the territory.
However, Shenzhen government officials said on Wednesday the planned erection of the six-metre (20-ft), six-tonne statue would be delayed -- possibly indefinitely.
Deng, who died in Beijing last February aged 92, had always said he would visit the territory for its return to Beijing rule at midnight on June 30 -- in a wheelchair if necessary.

The statue of the 150 cm (4 ft 11 ins) tall communist who ruled China for the last 18 years of his life was still being cast in Shanghai and would not be able to gaze over Hong Kong on July 1 as scheduled, Shenzhen officials said. They declined to give a reason for the delay.
"It's regrettable," sculptor Bai Lansheng said, but refused to say what was delaying the statue of the man who all his life abhorred the cult of personality.
